gaps.sentence: The delegates arrived early ___ have time to network.
gaps.explanation: 'So as to + infinitive' = in order to, a formal purpose linker.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.
'Due to personal reasons' is the standard collocation for giving a cause.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.
